correctness.rationale: Necessary and sufficient local conditions are reconstructed for both vertex kinds in a one-subdivision: E(H[U]) must be chosen and selected residual incidence at every unselected original vertex is at most one. Hence residual internal edges form a matching; each remaining original has 1+d_U(w)z cross choices. For K_n, choose the u originals, j matched outside pairs and remaining cross selections to derive A_n(z). Formal EGF via involution/matching exponential generating formula gives exp(t+t²/2+t exp(t)). For a proper set u<=n-1, selected residual edge-nodes inject into outside original capacities, giving size <=n+binom(u,2), sharp only at u=n-1 for n>=3. Actual adjacency enumeration independently verifies 75 host graphs of order <=4 and K2 to K6; 31 count coefficients match recurrence. Infinite proof does not rest on finite tests.

value.rationale: The 2026 primary paper identifies counting P3-convex sets as generally #P-hard and studies special tractable classes. The new all-host subdivision decomposition gives an explicit matching-polynomial bridge; specializing to complete hosts yields a compact infinite-family size polynomial and an entire-family labelled exponential generating function, not simply isolated computed counts. The exact rigid classification of all largest proper convex sets produces a nontrivial forbidden top-cardinality interval, a natural structural boundary of the closure system. This is motivated by the precise invariant on a canonical incidence-graph family, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
